title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
data_curation: Code RL tasks come from five pathways: GitHub PRs (with LLM-reconstructed issue specs when the issue is too thin), in-house employee 'vibe coding' requests, specification-driven tasks, CodeMidas source-derived tasks and agent-expanded long-horizon tasks, plus filtered public and vendor data. Supervision is checked by specification-test alignment review, a 4-rollout auditing agent that flags false positives and negatives, and F2P/P2P stability across 8 reruns. General-agent environments are resettable local sandboxes built from real files and multi-agent software mocks, scored with atomic binary rubrics (code checks plus LLM checks with cross-judge agreement) and hardened with adversarial solutions. Visual tasks are graded with pointwise and groupwise rubrics or pixel similarity. Cyber tasks are OSS-Fuzz vulnerability reproduction, where a PoC must match the sanitizer's bug type and top project stack frame. A hack agent probes environments for exploits until none remain. The RL mix is 68% coding, 12% tool use, 13% aesthetic design, 3% context following and 4% cyber.
curriculum: Two-stage pretraining: text first, then omni-modal joint training with an in-house ViT (4T+ image tokens) and an audio encoder, with context extended from 32K to 256K. Flash sees 48T tokens (26T text + 22T omni) and Pro sees 30T (27T + 3T). Agent-centric mid-training then runs at 256K and finally 1M context, switches hidden matrices from AdamW to the Muown optimizer, applies MXFP4 QAT, and adds reward-hacking self-correction examples. A short SFT follows. A single large mixed-task RL run ('You Only RL Once', about 30 steps) comes next, and MOPD2 multi-teacher on-policy distillation then merges domain teachers, including SFT teachers for hard-to-verify open domains.
method: Hybrid MoE with 128-token sliding-window attention interleaved with global attention and no shared experts: Pro has 1.02T total / 42B active parameters (384 experts, top-8), Flash 310B / 15B (256 experts). A DFlash block-diffusion drafter handles speculative decoding. RL is asynchronous GRPO with 1,568 prompts x 16 rollouts (25K trajectories, 2.7-3.7B tokens per step) at up to 1M context, partial rollout with staleness 4, a dynamic sampler, and prompt-mean loss aggregation. Optimization uses Muown at LR 3e-6. Four decoupled IS clip bounds start at [0.2, 5.0] and are tuned online from entropy. The MoE router is frozen. R3 routing replay, top-p candidate-set replay and MXFP4 QDQ keep training and inference consistent. Groupwise agentic grading has two parts: GRS multiplies the test reward by offline solution and behavior rubric scores, and GAR uses an online grader to rank passing patches, zero out confirmed hacks and redistribute positive advantage. A group-relative length penalty and segment-level penalties target format and tool errors. Infrastructure includes the Harness Pool, Payload Porter and Sample Mixer, with multi-harness training on minimal mini-harnesses.
eval_metrics: Coding benchmarks: DeepSWE v1.1, ProgramBench and internal MiMo Code Bench. Cyber: CyberGym (with corrected environments), ExploitGym, ExploitBench, SEC Bench Pro and MiMo Cyber Bench. General agent: AutomationBench, Toolathlon-Verified, GDPval-AA 2.1, Agents' Last Exam, Terminal-Bench 4.0/2.1, OSWorld-Verified and JobBench. Visual: MiMo Visual Coding. Baselines run at max reasoning effort. MiMo-V2.6-Pro scores: DeepSWE 71.9, ProgramBench 26.5, AutomationBench 53.1, Toolathlon-V 76.9, GDPval-AA 1673, Terminal-Bench 2.1 89.9, OSWorld-V 82.0, CyberGym 94.0, ExploitBench 47.9, SEC Bench Pro 66.3, Visual Coding 72.3. DeepSWE avg@3 over RL rose from 58.4 to 72.6 for Pro and from 48.7 to 65.7 for Flash. The open 9B distill reports SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (avg@3/avg@1).
key_results: About $2.6M of RL compute (43.8% rollout, 43.5% training, 12.7% grading) raises MiMo-V2.6-Pro's DeepSWE score from 58.4 to 72.6, against 19.0 for MiMo-V2.5-Pro and 74.0 for Claude Opus 5, and lifts held-out-harness pass@1 from about 50% to 66%. Freezing the router prevents load collapse (with a trainable router, CV rises from 0.78 to 2.0 and cold experts reach 22%), and confirmed hacking stays below 2% of trajectories. The open MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B plus RL reaches 66.2 on SWE-bench Verified and 52.8 on Terminal-Bench 2.1.
evolution_note: Builds on MiMo-V2-Flash's hybrid-SWA backbone, MOPD and RL infrastructure. It also adopts DAPO-style dynamic sampling, Kimi k1.5 partial rollout and R3 routing replay. It moves from verifiable-reward RLVR toward spending compute on agentic graders (GRS/GAR) that judge solution quality and behavior rather than only test pass/fail. It also adds systematic defenses against solution leakage and reward hacking. Releasing the 9B distill, the environments and the RL framework gives the open community a reproducible baseline for agentic RL.
